chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
I ate a meal with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I could not count how many times he said: 'The Praise is to Allah, Who made me desire it.'

key_terms.أَشْتَهِيهِ: I desire it / have an appetite for it

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet's family say before or during eating to show gratitude?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s profound mindfulness (muraqabah) by attributing the physical capacity to enjoy food—appetite—to Divine grace rather than mere biological function. In Shia scholarly tradition, this emphasizes that gratitude extends beyond the sustenance itself to the faculties that allow one to partake in it, reinforcing the spiritual dimension of daily acts like eating. It serves as a practical model for transforming mundane consumption into an act of worship through continuous remembrance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,
‘I ate a meal with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I could not count how many times he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Made me<sup>asws</sup> desire it’.
en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “
I ate food with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and I do not know how many times he (the Imam) said, ‘All praise belongs to Allah who has made me to have the appetite for food.’”
